topic: How do vaccines actually train your immune system to fight real viruses?
title: How Vaccines Work: Immune Memory Explained
false_sentence: Step three: specialized white blood cells become memory cells, storing the exact shape of that antibody.
correct_version: Memory cells do not store the shape of the antibody; they store the genetic information required to produce those specific antibodies upon re-exposure to the antigen.
why: The narration incorrectly suggests memory cells store the antibody shape, rather than the immunological blueprint for producing them.
